parsed.explanation: The text states the two uncancelled arrays have combined total T - d = 2(2^s - 1)d, and simultaneously that each has total at most (2^s - 1)d. Together these force each array to have total exactly (2^s - 1)d, an equality that the sweep-and-cancel procedure does not generally produce (the split of uncancelled portions between the two parity rows depends on the geometry of the columns, not just their sum). Hence the stated bound cannot both be the per-array bound and the combined bound, and the induction premise ('an array with at most s column-blocks and total at most (2^s-1)d') is unjustified. Moreover, 'arrays' and 'column-blocks' are never defined, and no argument shows cuts on these derived arrays correspond to legal splits of actual pieces. Lemma (i) is the sole engine of the all-n upper bound (Section 4), so the proof is incomplete/invalid as written.
